heading: SVX2 FastROM Animated Video
lede: Two complete Artemis videos: 600 frames of NASA SVS launch-and-return animation followed by 300 frames of real launch-camera footage, decoded at a verified 30 fps from a 4 MiB Fast HiROM.
keysHtml: Self-running — continuously plays both videos and switches codec keyframe and palette state at the frame-600 cut.
doc:
Two videos, one cartridge

Frames 0–599 are the NASA SVS Artemis launch-and-return animation; frames 600–899 are real Artemis I press-site camera footage. Each video has its own 223-color palette and begins with an independent SVX2 keyframe. The cartridge changes palette by DMA at the cut without disturbing the HDMA-owned dashboard split.

Cartridge-native dashboard

The SNES changes PPU modes at scanline 192: Mode 7 presents the video above, while conventional Mode 1 BG3 renders TIME, measured FPS, and health below. Nothing is burned into the footage.

30 fps full-pipeline result

The 4 MiB Fast HiROM contains 900 frames / 30 seconds in 2,355,828 SVX2 bytes. The regression records 1,928 presentations in 6,500 VBlanks, covers two complete 900-frame loops, and reports zero decoder errors and zero deadline slips.

Sources: NASA SVS 14191 animation and NASA Artemis I press-site camera footage. No Duck and Cover footage is present. Hit Verify fidelity to run the two-video target gate.
